answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-bound recurring work: every agent identity must lock reusable capital and publish a small proof-of-task tied to a recent checkpoint, like carrying a lotus upstream across a river and stamping marble with a fresh checkpoint mark. One operator can still make many accounts, but each clone needs separately locked stake, consumes time and compute, and is slashable if its proofs correlate. Mass fabrication therefore changes from free account creation into financing a visible fleet that loses capital whenever synchronized behavior is exposed.
